headline: Booking a Black Friday holiday? The CAA warns AI is making fake deals look real
summary: The UK Civil Aviation Authority says criminals are using AI to make fake holiday offers look genuine ahead of Black Friday on 27 November. UK customers lost £11m to holiday fraud in 2024.
body: The UK Civil Aviation Authority has warned holidaymakers to watch for fake travel deals in the run-up to Black Friday on 27 November and Travel Tuesday on 1 December. It says AI fakery is being used to lure shoppers into handing over their money.

City of London Police backs the warning. Chief Superintendent Amanda Wolf, head of Report Fraud operations, said criminals use “sophisticated websites, adverts and social media posts, sometimes enhanced by AI technology, to make fake holiday offers appear genuine.” Victims can end up paying for flights, accommodation or package holidays that don’t exist.

UK customers lost £11m to holiday fraud in 2024, according to City of London Police figures. The CAA says a professional-looking website or a padlock symbol doesn’t mean a travel company is genuine. Check the web address for misspellings or extra characters, and be wary of prices far below everyone else’s.
If you book a package holiday that includes flights, the company must hold an ATOL licence. If an ATOL firm stops trading, the scheme protects you from being stranded abroad or losing your money.
do_this: Before you pay for a package holiday, check the company holds an ATOL and the trip is ATOL protected at atol.org. You should get an ATOL Certificate when you book.
Pay by credit card, not bank transfer. Section 75 of the Consumer Credit Act may get you a refund on purchases between £100 and £30,000 if something goes wrong.
If you think you’ve been caught out, call your bank straight away, then report it at reportfraud.police.uk or on 0300 123 2040. In Scotland, call Police Scotland on 101.
source_name: the UK Civil Aviation Authority’s warning
